# Professional Tax in India 2026: State Wise Slab Rates, Due Dates, and Employer Compliance Guide


October 16, 2026


[Shashank Yadav](https://salarybox.in/blog/author/shashank87cc9f270b/)


[No comments yet](https://salarybox.in/blog/professional-tax-in-india-2026-state-wise-slab-rates-due-dates-and-employer-compliance-guide/#respond)


Every salaried employee in India has seen “Professional Tax” or “PT” as a deduction on their salary slip. Yet most employees do not know why it varies from state to state, and most employers are unsure which state’s rules apply to their business.


Professional Tax is one of the few taxes that state governments collect directly. Each state sets its own slab rates, due dates, and rules. There is no single national rate. This means a company with employees across multiple states must track different slab structures, different payment portals, and different deadlines.


This guide covers everything about Professional Tax for FY 2026-27. Whether you are an employee trying to understand the deduction on your payslip or an employer managing[payroll compliance](https://salarybox.in/blog/payroll-compliance-checklist-for-indian-smes-2025-update/) across states, you will find complete state wise slab tables, registration steps, due dates, penalties, and exemptions here.


## What Is Professional Tax?


Professional Tax (PT) is a state level tax on income earned through employment, profession, trade, or calling. Despite the name, it applies to everyone who earns an income, not just “professionals.”


Detail Description


What it taxes Income from salary, profession, trade, or calling


Who levies it State governments and union territories


Constitutional basis Article 276(2) of the Indian Constitution


Maximum annual limit ₹2,500 per person per year


Who pays it Employee (deducted from salary) and employer (separate payment)


Who deducts from salary Employer deducts and deposits on behalf of employee


Is it tax deductible Yes, allowed as deduction from salary under Section 16(iii) of Income Tax Act


Applicability Salaried employees, self-employed professionals, business owners, freelancers


Governing law Individual state acts (e.g., Maharashtra State Tax on Professions Act, 1975)


**Key point:** The ₹2,500 annual cap comes from Article 276(2) of the Constitution. No state can charge more than ₹2,500 per year per person. Some states collect the full ₹2,500, while others collect less.

## Complete State Wise Professional Tax Slab Rates


Here are the detailed slab tables for every state that levies Professional Tax. Bookmark this section because it is the reference you will keep coming back to.


### Maharashtra Professional Tax Slabs


Maharashtra is the most common state for PT queries. It has a unique structure where the February payment is higher than other months.


Monthly Gross Salary PT Per Month


Up to ₹7,500 Nil

Above ₹10,000 ₹200 (₹300 in February)


Key Detail Information


Maximum Annual PT ₹2,500 (₹200 x 11 months + ₹300 in February)


Women Exemption Women earning up to ₹25,000/month are exempt


Payment Due Date Last day of the month


Registration Portal mahagst.gov.in


Governing Law Maharashtra State Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1975


**Why February is different:** Maharashtra collects ₹200 per month for 11 months (₹2,200) and ₹300 in February to reach the ₹2,500 annual maximum.

## Employer Registration: PTRC and PTEC Explained


As an employer, you need two types of Professional Tax registrations in most states:


### PTRC vs PTEC


Registration Full Name Purpose Who Needs It


PTRC Professional Tax Registration Certificate To deduct PT from employee salaries and deposit it with the state Every employer with employees in PT applicable states


PTEC Professional Tax Enrolment Certificate For employer’s own PT liability as a business entity Every business owner, professional, or self-employed person


**Important:** These are two separate registrations. An employer needs PTRC to deduct and remit employee PT, and PTEC for their own personal PT obligation. Missing either one attracts penalties.


### Registration Process (General Steps)


Step Action Documents Needed


1 Visit state commercial tax portal PAN of company/proprietor


2 Fill online application form Certificate of Incorporation or GST registration


3 Upload supporting documents Address proof of business premises


4 Pay registration fee (if applicable) Bank account details


5 Submit application Identity proof of authorized signatory


6 Receive PTRC/PTEC number Mobile number and email for OTP verification

### Real Impact: Penalty Calculation Example


**Scenario:** A company in Maharashtra with 50 employees, each earning above ₹10,000/month, fails to deposit PT for 6 months.


Calculation Amount


Monthly PT per employee ₹200


Total monthly PT for 50 employees ₹10,000


PT for 6 months (not deposited) ₹60,000


Interest at 1.25% per month (average 3 months) ₹2,250


Late filing penalty (6 returns x ₹1,000) ₹6,000


**Total liability** **₹68,250**


Beyond financial penalties, repeated non compliance can lead to:


1. Prosecution under the state PT act
2. Assessment proceedings by the state tax authority
3. Seizure of business assets in severe cases (Maharashtra)
4. Difficulty obtaining compliance certificates for government contracts

### Standard Exemptions (Common Across Most States)


Category Exemption States Where Applicable


Income below threshold Fully exempt if salary is below the first slab All PT states


Armed Forces personnel Fully exempt All states

Persons with physical disability (40% or more) Fully exempt Most states


Badli (substitute) workers Exempt in some states Maharashtra, Gujarat


Senior citizens (above 65) Exempt Select states


### State Specific Exemptions


State Special Exemption


Maharashtra Women earning up to ₹25,000/month are exempt


Karnataka Employees earning up to ₹25,000/month are exempt (applies to all genders)


West Bengal Persons with disability holding certificate under RPD Act are exempt


Tamil Nadu Agriculturists and educational institutions are exempt


**Note on Maharashtra Women’s Exemption:** This is one of the most frequently asked questions. In Maharashtra, women employees whose monthly salary does not exceed ₹25,000 are exempt from Professional Tax. Women earning above ₹25,000 pay PT at the normal slab rates. This exemption does not apply to self-employed women professionals, who pay PT based on their income.

Employee on deputation State of the deputing company


Contract worker State where work is performed


### Compliance Checklist for Multi State Employers


Task Frequency Details

## Professional Tax and Income Tax: How PT Affects Your Tax


Professional Tax affects your income tax in two ways:


### Deduction Under Section 16(iii)


Item Details


Section 16(iii) of the Income Tax Act


Deduction Allowed Full amount of PT paid during the year


Available in Old Tax Regime Yes


Available in New Tax Regime Yes


Where it appears in Form 16 Part B, under “Deductions from Salary”


Maximum deduction ₹2,500 (the most any state charges)


**Important:** Professional Tax is deductible under both old and new tax regimes. This is one of the very few deductions available in the new regime.


### Impact on TDS Calculation


Your employer considers PT when calculating monthly TDS. Here is an example:


Item Without PT Deduction With PT Deduction


Annual Gross Salary ₹10,00,000 ₹10,00,000


Standard Deduction ₹75,000 ₹75,000


Professional Tax ₹0 ₹2,500


Taxable Income ₹9,25,000 ₹9,22,500


Tax Payable (New Regime) ₹32,500 ₹32,250


**Tax Saving from PT Deduction** **₹250**


The tax saving from PT deduction is modest (₹250 to ₹750 depending on your slab rate), but it reduces your TDS every month. Your employer should be accounting for this in your monthly[salary slip](https://salarybox.in/salary-slip-generator/) .


For more details on how TDS works with salary deductions, refer to our[TDS on salaries guide](https://salarybox.in/blog/tds-on-salaries-a-comprehensive-guide-for-employers/) .

## Odisha Professional Tax Abolition: What Employers Need to Know


Odisha became the first state to abolish Professional Tax in FY 2026-27. Here is what changed:


Item Before April 1, 2026 From April 1, 2026


PT Status Levied (max ₹2,500/year) Abolished


Employee Deduction Required for employees above threshold Not required


PTRC/PTEC Required for employers No longer required


Pending Dues Must be cleared All dues up to March 31, 2026 must be settled


Returns Must be filed No further returns needed


Salary Impact ₹125 to ₹208/month deduction No deduction (employees get slightly higher take home pay)


**Action items for Odisha employers:**


1. Stop PT deduction from April 2026 salary onwards
2. Update your[payroll system](https://salarybox.in/blog/how-to-improve-payroll-efficiency-with-automated-software-solutions/) to remove PT for Odisha employees
3. File final PT return for the period up to March 2026
4. Clear any pending PT dues for previous periods
5. Inform employees about the change (marginally higher take home salary)

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)


**1. What is Professional Tax and who has to pay it?**


Professional Tax is a state level tax levied on income earned from salary, profession, trade, or calling. Every salaried employee working in a state that levies PT has it deducted from their salary by their employer. Self-employed professionals, business owners, and freelancers in PT states must also pay PT through their own PTEC registration. The employer deducts PT from employee salaries and deposits it with the state government. The maximum PT any state can charge is ₹2,500 per year, as mandated by Article 276(2) of the Constitution.


**2. Which states in India do not levy Professional Tax?**


As of FY 2026-27, the following states and union territories do not levy Professional Tax: Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Haryana, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Goa, Chandigarh, Andaman and Nicobar, Lakshadweep, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. Punjab has a State Development Tax that functions similarly but PT itself is suspended. Odisha abolished Professional Tax from April 1, 2026, so it no longer applies there.


**3. Is Professional Tax the same in all states?**


No. Each state sets its own slab rates, exemption thresholds, and payment schedules. For example, Maharashtra charges up to ₹2,500 per year with the first slab starting at ₹7,500 monthly salary, while Karnataka exempts everyone earning below ₹25,000 per month and charges a maximum of ₹2,400 per year. Some states collect PT monthly, some half yearly, and some annually. The due dates also vary from the 10th of the following month (Andhra Pradesh) to the last day of the month (Maharashtra).


**4. Can I claim Professional Tax as a deduction in my income tax return?**


Yes. Professional Tax is allowed as a deduction under Section 16(iii) of the Income Tax Act. This deduction is available in both the old and new tax regimes. It appears in Part B of your Form 16 under “Deductions from Salary.” Your employer should already be accounting for PT when computing your monthly TDS. The maximum deduction is ₹2,500 (the constitutional cap), and it reduces your taxable income by that amount.


**5. What happens if my employer does not deduct Professional Tax from my salary?**


If your employer does not deduct PT in a state that requires it, the employer faces penalties, not the employee. The employer can be charged interest on late payment (typically 1% to 2% per month), a penalty for non registration, and late filing fees for missed returns. In severe cases, the state tax authority can initiate prosecution. If you notice PT is not being deducted from your salary in a state that levies it, bring it to your employer’s attention. The employer is legally responsible for deduction and deposit.


**6. I work remotely from a state different from my company’s office. Which state’s PT applies?**


Professional Tax is generally applicable based on where the employee works, not where the company is registered. If you work remotely from Karnataka and your company is registered in Maharashtra, Karnataka’s PT rules apply to your salary. Your employer should register for PT in Karnataka and apply Karnataka’s slab rates to your salary. However, implementation varies and some employers apply PT based on the office location. The legally correct approach is to apply PT based on the employee’s work location.


**7. How is Professional Tax different from Income Tax?**


Professional Tax is a state level tax with a maximum cap of ₹2,500 per year. Income Tax is a central government tax with no cap on the amount (it can go up to 30% plus surcharge and cess). PT is a fixed amount based on salary slabs. Income Tax is calculated on total taxable income after all deductions. PT is deducted monthly by the employer and deposited with the state. Income Tax is managed through TDS (monthly) and ITR filing (annually). Both are separate obligations and paying one does not exempt you from the other.


**8. My company has employees in 5 different states. Do we need separate PT registration in each state?**


Yes. You need a separate PTRC (Professional Tax Registration Certificate) in each state where you have employees. Each state has its own registration portal and process. You must apply the correct slab rates for each state, follow each state’s payment due dates, and file returns as per each state’s requirements. For a company with employees in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, and West Bengal, this means tracking 5 different slab structures, 5 different due dates, and filing returns on 5 different portals. This is one of the key reasons businesses use[automated payroll software](https://salarybox.in/blog/how-to-improve-payroll-efficiency-with-automated-software-solutions/) that handles multi state PT compliance automatically.
